title: Calibration Lab Notebook: Crosswalk for Multi-Workload Evaluations
author: Nadia Cortez
body:
Overview

This lab notebook describes a practical crosswalk for calibrating evaluation fidelity across heterogeneous workloads. It documents provenance mapping, sampling budgets, annotation/labeler contracts, quantization interaction checks, and regression-triage thresholds so that model onboarding, shadow validations, and periodic audits share a single source of truth. The target audience is applied-ML engineers, evaluators, and platform owners who operate the eval harness and manage model promotion.

Why this document exists

- Multiple teams run separate evaluations (shadow, canary, offline suites) that produce conflicting signals.
- Differences in prompt selection, batch sizes, tokenization, and quant profiles create non-trivial delta in measured metrics.
- When regressions occur we need a reproducible path from a failing customer slice back to a minimal repro evaluation.

Scope

This notebook covers:
1) A canonical calibration matrix that maps workload characteristics to evaluation settings.
2) Sampling and budget rules for each evaluation class (smoke, fidelity, longtail, stress).
3) Annotator/labeler contract templates for behavioral and safety checks.
4) Quantization interaction checklist to detect artifacts introduced by lower-precision inference.
5) Regression triage triggers and triage playbook cross-reference.

Calibration matrix (canonical)

The matrix below captures recommended eval harness config per workload fingerprint. Use these values as defaults; deviation requires a documented justification.

- Workload fingerprint: short-chat-interactive (median prompt tokens < 40)
  - Eval class: smoke + micro-fidelity
  - Batch size: 1–4 (preserve latency SLOs)
  - KV cache: warm and cold runs (50/50 split)
  - Quant profile: FP16 baseline + int8 sanity
  - Sampling: stratified across top-10 intents, 200 samples per intent

- Workload fingerprint: long-context-recall (median prompt tokens 1024–4096)
  - Eval class: longtail + stability
  - Batch size: 2–8 (prefer small to avoid OOM)
  - KV cache: forced cold starts only
  - Quant profile: FP16 + mixed-precision candidate
  - Sampling: focused slices by context-length bins, 500 total samples

- Workload fingerprint: high-throughput-embeddings
  - Eval class: throughput-fidelity
  - Batch size: 256–1024 (in harness simulated batched producer)
  - Quant profile: int8 quantized embedding kernels
  - Sampling: synthetic and real mix, 10k vectors for perf, 1k for embedding drift

- Workload fingerprint: instruction-following-open-domain
  - Eval class: fidelity + safety-sentinel
  - Batch size: 8–32 for cost-fidelity tradeoffs
  - Quant profile: FP16 baseline, int8 must pass acceptance checks
  - Sampling: balanced across instruction templates, 1k–2k samples for release candidates

Sampling and budget rules

- Smoke evaluations: max 1k tokens / model-run, nightly. Purpose: surface obvious regressions.
- Fidelity evaluations: 1–5k labeled examples depending on release risk (higher for public-facing models).
- Longtail/stress: heavy but targeted — only run when promoting to Dedicated or Private or when telemetry indicates increased failure rate for a slice. Budget: 10–50k calls per month per model family.
- Canary/shadow: mirror production traffic for 24–72 hours with a 1:1000 sample ratio for high-volume customers; increase to 1:100 for critical enterprise tenants during initial onboarding.

Annotator / labeler contract (template)

The annotator contract ensures consistency across teams and time. Key fields:
- Objective: the metric(s) being labeled (e.g., helpfulness, instruction-follow correctness, hallucination_present boolean).
- Annotation schema version: semantic version string (e.g., v1.4.0).
- Inter-annotator agreement target: Cohen's kappa >= 0.75 for binary judgments, Krippendorff alpha >= 0.7 for multi-class.
- Minimum context: full prompt + previous 2 turns for multi-turn judgments.
- Labeler qualification: pass gold set at >= 85% before labeling.
- Escalation: ambiguous or safety-tagged items -> safety review queue within 24 hours.

Checklist: quantization interaction tests

Quantization often changes distributional behavior. The following automated checks must be part of the promotion pipeline whenever a quantized runtime is evaluated:
- Deterministic delta check: compare token-level logprobs across FP16 and candidate quantized run on 1k anchor prompts. Threshold: median KL divergence per-token < 0.02.
- Output-stability check: run 3 seeds with same prompts through quantized runtime; token-level edit distance variance threshold < 6% relative to FP16.
- Behavioral regression test: critical intent set (100 seeds) must not drop intent accuracy by > 2 percentage points.
- Safety-sentinel pass rate: must meet the same guardrail thresholds used in production (see quality-guardrails page).
- KV cache integrity: ensure cached state is consistent between FP16 and quantized runtimes on a 200-case sequence replay test.

Operational procedures: from failing telemetry to minimal repro

1) Triage trigger
   - When production telemetry shows a slice breach (response_stability_index delta > 0.12 OR latency P95 regression > 1.5x baseline) an incident ticket is opened by telemetry-scan.
2) Snapshot collection (owner: eval-harness-oncall)
   - Export 500 example sessions from the offending slice (preserve request metadata, model_version, routing_policy).
   - Record runtime config: batch_size, quant_profile, GPU kernel selection, model weights hash.
3) Prioritized repro path (owner: applied-ml-evals)
   - Re-run samples across three environments: FP16 baseline, candidate quantized runtime, and production runtime at same model_version.
   - Use deterministic seeds and tokenization flags identical to production.
4) Root cause checks
   - Diff outputs using semantic similarity metrics (ROUGE-L, BERTScore, normalized edit distance) and token-prob divergence.
   - If differences map to quantization-induced divergence, escalate to quant-profiles team.
   - If differences map to prompt drift or new user-intent patterns, create a prompt augmentation backlog item.
5) Remediation and promotion
   - If regression is confirmed and impacts SLOs, revert rollout or apply fallback routing policy (route to FP16 variant).
   - Author a regression triage summary with minimal repro steps and attach to the incident.

CLI and YAML examples (canonical configs)

# Example eval harness run (shell)
# Run fidelity suite with int8 candidate profile

- command: |
  eval-harness run \
    --suite fidelity \
    --model redwood-xl-2 \
    --quant-profile int8-candidate-v2 \
    --batch-size 8 \
    --seed 42 \
    --out results/redwood-xl-2-int8-v2.json

# Example minimal promotion YAML (eval job)
---
name: promotion-eval
model: redwood-xl-2
variant: int8-candidate-v2
suite: fidelity
samples: 2000
checks:
  - name: token-kl-threshold
    metric: median_token_kl
    threshold: 0.02
  - name: intent-accuracy-drop
    metric: intent_accuracy_delta
    threshold: -0.02
rollout_actions:
  on_fail: fallback-to: fp16-baseline
  on_pass: proceed-to-canary

Ownership, SLAs and metrics to monitor

- Owners: applied-ml-evals (primary), runtime-quant (secondary), platform-oncall (escalation).
- SLOs for evaluation platform: job_success_rate >= 99% (daily), median_run_time for fidelity suite < 90 minutes.
- Key telemetry: response_stability_index, intent_accuracy_delta, median_token_kl, safety_sentinel_fail_rate.

Notes on reproducibility and provenance

- Every eval job must attach an immutable provenance blob: model_weights_hash, tokenizer_version, runtime_kernels, and hardware SKU. Store in S3 under eval-provenance/YYYY/MM/DD/{job_id}.json.
- Use the eval-harness --provenance flag to auto-capture environment metadata.

Appendix: quick checklists

Pre-promotion checklist (applied-ml-evals):
- [ ] Smoke pass on nightly harness
- [ ] Fidelity suite within thresholds
- [ ] Quantization interaction tests green
- [ ] Annotator gold-set agreement verified
- [ ] Provenance blob stored and linked

On regression detection (first 24 hours):
- [ ] Snapshot exported
- [ ] Repro across FP16, quant candidate, production run
- [ ] Triage summary created and linked to incident
- [ ] Rollback or routing policy applied if SLO breached
